summary.headline: Aurum PropTech Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue rose 10.2% QoQ to INR 123.85 crores, with second straight profitable quarter and FY26 revenue up 50.8% to INR 381.09 crores.
summary.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as an inflection point: second consecutive PAT-positive quarter, operating leverage starting to show, and debt retirement planned by June 30, 2026 via sale of buildings. Continuing-operations PBT was INR 1.85 crores in Q4 versus INR 2.93 crores in Q3, so profitability is still thin on a pre-tax basis. Distribution was the main growth engine, with PropTiger reporting its highest-ever quarterly gross commission of INR 42.8 crores. Management reiterated AI-first positioning (business value optimization and a longer-term "Unified Brain") but gave few quantified AI outcomes; the first measurable target is revenue per team member.

segments.name: Rental (continuing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 52.70 crores vs INR 52.09 crores in Q3; segment loss INR 3.61 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 200.71 crores, +27.4% YoY, with segment loss INR 18.54 crores. Including discontinued building operations, Q4 rental revenue was INR 55.20 crores and combined loss INR 2.74 crores.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 66.87 crores vs INR 59.60 crores in Q3 (+12.2%); segment profit INR 13.63 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 172.55 crores, +117.7% YoY, with segment profit INR 32.30 crores. Management cites 22-25% segment margins.

segments.name: Capital
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 4.28 crores vs INR 0.67 crores in Q3; segment loss INR 0.53 crores in Q4. FY26 revenue INR 7.84 crores vs INR 15.94 crores in FY25 (down), segment loss INR 5.27 crores.

segments.name: PropTiger (within distribution)
segments.commentary: Highest-ever quarterly gross commission of INR 42.8 crores in Q4 FY26; 175 active developer clients and 11 active mandates; developer relationships cited at 180+.

segments.name: Aurum Analytica (within distribution)
segments.commentary: Sold over 1,48,000 leads in Q4 FY26 (+93% YoY) to 145 active clients across 275 signed projects; active accounts +23% and projects +20% YoY. Later answer cited 1,20,000 leads, an inconsistent figure.

segments.name: Sell.do (within distribution)
segments.commentary: 916 active accounts (+38% YoY) and 10,378 active licenses (+32% YoY) at Q4 end; 40+ new developers and 600+ new licenses added in the quarter.

segments.name: HelloWorld (rental)
segments.commentary: 259 active co-living properties (+13% YoY) and 19,286 beds under management (+9% YoY). Management says HelloWorld reached adjusted EBITDA break-even in the current month.

segments.name: NestAway (rental)
segments.commentary: About 9,600 rentable units across 5,214 houses at Q4 end; house count declined YoY after portfolio rationalisation. NestAway Select premium cluster model launched in Q4. Management targets rental profitability in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management said it could not give forward-looking statements but expects growth of about 40% YoY to continue over the next three years, citing a 40% revenue CAGR since inception.
Sale of buildings expected to retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026; surplus cash to fund AI initiatives over the next couple of years.
Company expects to cross INR 1,000 crores annualised revenue in coming quarters (current run-rate cited at around INR 500 crores).
Rental profitability trends expected to emerge in FY27; HelloWorld already at adjusted EBITDA break-even.
Management expects higher adjusted EBITDA and PBT margins in coming quarters from AI-driven automation; revenue per team member to be tracked as the key AI metric.
SM REIT (commercial, pre-leased Grade A assets) targeted for launch within FY27 across Mumbai, Pune, Delhi NCR, Bangalore and Ahmedabad.
capex_capacity: Sale of buildings: partial sale recognised INR 17.72 crores other income; Q5 and Q6 buildings sale is expected to clear lease rental discounting debt by June 30, 2026.
Rental portfolio: about 30,000 beds under management across HelloWorld and NestAway combined; growth planned via beds and higher-value rental revenue streams.
NestAway Select (premium cluster-based rental) launched in Q4 FY26 in high-demand micro-markets.
SM REIT pipeline being built; pre-leased commercial assets under evaluation, with detailed due diligence pending.
Win a Pin Code strategy: supply concentrated in pin codes with robust momentum for student living, co-living and family rentals.
demand_pricing: PropTiger shifting from transaction model to mandate (exclusive) model; management says mandates carry higher gross commission and margins than standard brokerage.
Distribution segment (PropTiger, Analytica, Sell.do) contributes around 60% of total income, per management.
Cross-sell: about 22% of the distribution network uses multiple products; management says ecosystem cross-sell revenue is still in single digits as a share of revenue and is now being tracked.
Management cited a addressable industry spend of INR 38,000 crores by developers in top eight cities on lead generation, aggregators and transaction management.
Rental demand headwinds in IT cities: Pune weaker (BPO-dependent), Bangalore relatively resilient; management says quality pin code selection offsets this.

qa_highlights.question: How will AI be implemented, and what are the capital allocation priorities after the building sale?
qa_highlights.answer: AI split into business value optimisation (mapping rental, distribution and capital processes, with revenue per team member as the guiding metric) and a longer-term Unified Brain agentic layer on top of existing LLMs. Surplus proceeds after debt retirement will fund AI over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned, given PE/VC-backed peers may be divesting?
qa_highlights.answer: No active acquisition pipeline; management will only pursue deals that sit between two existing operating businesses. PropTiger was the example. Focus is organic growth plus SM REIT.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth organic, and how will rental and distribution grow given IT hiring slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution growth was partly inorganic via PropTiger (transaction concluded in Q2 FY26). Management sees rental growth from HelloWorld and NestAway via Win a Pin Code, and says distribution gains from developer lead-gen spend during slow sales cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NestAway house count decline YoY while the model is asset-light?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the decline to deliberate rationalisation and consolidation of houses; revenue rose due to value-added services at pin-code level. Rental profitability targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SM REIT timeline and focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on commercial pre-leased Grade A assets given SEBI rules; pipeline being built with channel partners; launch targeted within FY27 subject to due diligence.

qa_highlights.question: How are AI benefits measured versus operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Performance metrics (conversion, connection rates, time to go live) to be tracked over a few quarters, with revenue per employee as the net metric. Employee count excludes outsourced staff and interns.

qa_highlights.question: What are PAT margin prospects by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Distribution consistently profitable with 22-25% margins; rental still takes time due to NestAway platform, tech and go-to-market spend. HelloWorld near adjusted EBITDA break-even.

risks_watch: Continuing-operations PBT was only INR 1.85 crores in Q4 and the rental segment is loss-making (Q4 loss INR 3.61 crores); profitability depends on rental turning positive in FY27.
NestAway house count fell YoY; management's rationalisation claim needs confirmation in next quarter's unit numbers.
Rental demand exposure to IT and BPO hiring slowdown, especially in Pune; management concedes a dip in demand.
AI benefits unquantified: revenue per team member is the only stated net metric and will be tracked from the next quarters.
Capital segment revenue fell sharply in FY26 (INR 7.84 crores vs INR 15.94 crores).
Distribution revenue depends on developer sales cycles and the PropTiger mandate pipeline; cross-sell still single digit as a share of revenue.
Verify the building sale and June 30, 2026 debt retirement, and the SM REIT launch timing.
key_quotes: First, we are now a profitable company. And we believe this is not cyclical; we are structurally profitable.
The sale of buildings Q5 and Q6 will ensure that we retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026.

Nishita, we are not allowed to give forward -looking statements, but if you look at the last 4 years right from inception of Aurum PropTech and our PropTech business model, we've consistently delivered a growth of 40% year-on-year from a revenue standpoint.
Those numbers are still in single digit, and that is one focus that we have this year, to start evaluating internally that how much of the revenue is coming as a cross-sell revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, debt retirement and AI, with management repeatedly calling Q4 an inflection point. Cautious and evasive on forward numbers: it declined to give forward-looking statements, gave no quantified AI outcomes, and conceded rental demand weakness in Pune and single-digit cross-sell revenue.

adds.what: NestAway Select premium cluster rental model launched in Q4 FY26 (no unit count given)
SM REIT (commercial, pre-leased Grade A assets) targeted launch in FY27 across five cities; pipeline under evaluation, due diligence pending

growth.why: Management said it could not give formal guidance but expects roughly 40% YoY growth to continue over three years (FY27-FY29), citing 40% CAGR since inception; backing is qualitative (PropTiger mandates, record Q4 gross commission of INR 42.8 cr, Analytica lead growth +93%, SM REIT and NestAway Select launches) with no specific capacity or order numbers tied to the 40% target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects higher adjusted EBITDA and PBT margins from AI automation, distribution runs at 22-25% segment margins, and HelloWorld reached adjusted EBITDA break-even, though Q4 PBT was only INR 1.85 crores on INR 123.85 crores revenue.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity or capex plan; the only new supply is SM REIT launch targeted within FY27 with due diligence pending, and HelloWorld has 19,286 beds (+9% YoY) while NestAway house count fell YoY to about 5,214 houses.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Distribution revenue rose 12.2% QoQ to INR 66.87 crores, Analytica leads were up 93% YoY to over 1,48,000, and Sell.do active licenses rose 32% YoY to 10,378, though rental house count fell YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with capex not discussed; building sales are being used to retire lease rental discounting debt by June 30, 2026, and surplus cash is earmarked for AI rather than plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects about 40% YoY growth to continue over three years and FY26 revenue rose 50.8% to INR 381.09 crores, but it explicitly declined to give formal forward numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance and Q4 PBT fell to INR 1.85 crores from INR 2.93 crores in Q3 while rental still loses money (Q4 loss INR 3.61 crores), so profit delivery depends on rental turning positive in FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NestAway Select premium cluster rental was launched in Q4 FY26 and the SM REIT is targeted for launch within FY27 across five cities, though no unit count or size was disclosed.

rows.label: Lease rental discounting debt retired by June 30, 2026
rows.why: Management says partial building sale (INR 17.72 crores other income recognised) and Q5/Q6 building sales will retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026, though the sale was flagged for verification.

rows.label: PropTiger mandate shift
rows.why: PropTiger reported a record INR 42.8 crores gross commission in Q4 with 11 active mandates, and management says mandates carry higher commission and margins than transaction brokerage.

rows.label: Rental segment profitability
rows.why: Rental still lost INR 3.61 crores in Q4 on INR 52.70 crores revenue and HelloWorld is only at adjusted EBITDA break-even, so rental profit depends on FY27 execution.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, debt retirement and AI, but cautious on forward numbers, declining formal guidance and giving no quantified AI outcomes; analysts probed AI benefits, the inorganic PropTiger contribution, NestAway house count decline and rental profitability timing.
